newsitem.title: FINLAND: HIGH-COST AIRLINES CANNOT SURVIVE - FINNAIR.
newsitem.headline: HIGH-COST AIRLINES CANNOT SURVIVE - FINNAIR.

text.p: High-cost airlines will not survive long in Europe's soon-to-be deregulated markets, Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy said in a company newsletter received on Tuesday.
Finnair said it would not be possible to increase staff, but it also said the main target of an earlier announced programme to cut costs was not to implement harsh personnel reductions.

"The fight for survival and profitability is tough," Finnair CEO Antti Potila told a staff meeting as he presented the programme, the newsletter wrote. "High-cost airlines will not survive long," Finnair personnel director Juhani Suomela said.
Referring to the opening of European skies on April 1, Suomela said cost-efficient low-fare carriers like Virgin Express were entering the market.
"Traditional airlines are cutting their own fares to be competitive and retain or even increase market shares," he said.
"Essential changes must take place to succeed in a deregulated Europe as a company paying dividend to its owners and ensuring the jobs of its employees," he added.
Under is own programme, Finnair is looking hard at all operations with the aim to cut costs and boost revenue for an annual earnings improvement of 500 million markka.

"The target is not just a sketch, the 500 million markka total is made up of small parts," the newsletter said, adding the group was in for a treatment focussing on tangible measures instead of speeches and plans.
"The measures are permanent, we want them to have an enduring effect on Finnair's earnings in the long term," Potila said.

Finnair's annual staff costs are nearly two billion markka. "Increasing staff entails costs which are not possible in this situation," the newsletter said. "A sharp reduction in staff is not a primary concern now," it added.
